item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"c1","claim_type":"core","weight":18,"statement":"The program defines a Pydantic `BaseModel` for `event_info` with nested data and uses `event_info: CalendarEvent` both in the tool function and in the DSPy signature/input path.","span_ids":["e4","e5"]},{"claim_id":"c2","claim_type":"core","weight":22,"statement":"The example uses `DummyLM` to script exactly one real tool call with JSON-like `next_tool_args`, then a `finish` call with empty args, then a final extraction response, and runs that transcript through `dspy.ReAct`.","span_ids":["e4","e5"]},{"claim_id":"c3","claim_type":"core","weight":30,"statement":"The program explicitly verifies that the live Python tool invocation receives a parsed `CalendarEvent` object for `event_info`, not the raw dict emitted by the LM.","span_ids":["e1","e2","e3"]},{"claim_id":"c4","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"The program asserts that the returned `trajectory` preserves the original LM-emitted tool arguments as plain nested dict data under `tool_args_0`, and that the trajectory also records the subsequent `finish` step.","span_ids":["e3","e6"]},{"claim_id":"c5","claim_type":"supporting","weight":10,"statement":"The program checks the final `invitation_letter` value and prints the tool-side type evidence alongside `result.trajectory[\"tool_args_0\"]` so the dict-vs-model distinction is visible at runtime.","span_ids":["e3","e5","e6"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"e1","path":"dspy/adapters/types/tool.py","start_line":135,"end_line":146},{"span_id":"e2","path":"dspy/adapters/types/tool.py","start_line":177,"end_line":179},{"span_id":"e3","path":"dspy/predict/react.py","start_line":105,"end_line":115},{"span_id":"e4","path":"tests/predict/test_react.py","start_line":58,"end_line":75},{"span_id":"e5","path":"tests/predict/test_react.py","start_line":76,"end_line":114},{"span_id":"e6","path":"tests/predict/test_react.py","start_line":116,"end_line":133}]}
